actor: agent-platform security product manager at a major cloud provider or agent runtime vendor
job: Designing and shipping inline MCP-channel policy enforcement as a first-class default in an agent runtime, not as a bolt-on proxy.
outcome: A third major agent platform ships production-ready inline MCP-channel access control with per-agent scoped enforcement as a documented GA default.
motivation: Enterprises are demanding that agent tool invocations be policy-gated at the runtime layer; shipping this default captures the governance control point and accelerates enterprise adoption.

task.who: the platform security and agent-runtime product engineering team
task.what: implement per-agent scoped policy enforcement on MCP channels
task.where: the agent runtime's tool-invocation layer before network egress
task.why: capture enterprise demand for inline MCP policy before rivals lock in the pattern
task.how: a policy engine called by the agent runtime before any tool invocation leaves the process

actor: enterprise security architect evaluating agent platforms for production deployment
job: Requiring and piloting inline MCP-channel policy enforcement as a procurement criterion, creating pull demand on any platform that lacks it.
outcome: Enterprise buying pressure forces additional agent platforms to ship inline MCP policy enforcement as a default feature to remain competitive.
motivation: Ungoverned MCP calls crossing network boundaries are unacceptable under enterprise security policy; a platform default removes the need for custom bolt-on proxies.

task.who: the enterprise platform-security and agent-governance evaluation team
task.what: assess and require inline MCP policy enforcement in agent platform RFPs
task.where: vendor evaluations, security reviews, and enterprise procurement processes
task.why: enforce zero-trust posture on agent tool calls without bespoke proxy solutions
task.how: security requirements mapped to Zscaler AI Broker and Databricks Agent Bricks as reference implementations
